title: Can you remember…? 1
subtitle: Review practice: grammar, Social English, and clothes colours

blocks.title: Grammar
blocks.text: Complete the six sentences. Type the two missing words in each sentence.

blocks.title: 1. Complete the sentences
blocks.instructions: Type one word in each gap.

items.prompt: Complete the sentence.
segments: His name’s Enrique, but he’s called Kike
items.explanation: He’s called Kike for short.

items.prompt: Complete the sentence.
segments: This isn’t my jacket. That beige one
items.explanation: That beige one is mine.

items.prompt: Complete the sentence.
segments: This isn’t my book. A friend lent it
items.explanation: A friend lent it to me.

items.prompt: Complete the sentence.
segments: I’m not looking for expensive trainers; I want to buy some
items.explanation: I want to buy some cheap ones.

items.prompt: Complete the sentence.
segments: It takes me a lot longer to get to work now because I live
items.explanation: I live much further away than I used to.

items.prompt: Complete the sentence.
segments: My neighbours don’t look after their garden. Theirs is
items.explanation: Theirs is the least attractive garden in the street.

blocks.title: Social English
blocks.text: Complete the highlighted phrases, then use the phrases to finish the conversations.

blocks.title: 3a. Complete the highlighted phrases
blocks.instructions: Use a word from the list. Type only the missing word.

items.prompt: A: It’s lovely to see you. B: It’s ______ to see you, too.
items.explanation: It’s great to see you, too.

items.prompt: A: I can’t believe we’re here, Sophie. B: Neither can I. It’s ______, isn’t it?
items.explanation: It’s weird, isn’t it?

items.prompt: A: Look at this top I’ve just bought! B: Oh ______! It’s amazing!
items.explanation: Oh wow! It’s amazing!

items.prompt: A: I’ve lost my passport. B: It’s not your ______, is it?
items.explanation: It’s not your day, is it?

items.prompt: A: I really ______ you. B: Me too.
items.explanation: I really miss you.

items.prompt: A: They’ve cancelled my flight. B: Oh no! That’s ______.
items.explanation: That’s awful.

items.prompt: A: I’ll put my bag in my room. B: Please, let me ______ that for you.
items.explanation: Please, let me take that for you.

blocks.title: What the colour of your clothes says about you
blocks.text: Read the article and choose a, b, or c for each gap.

blocks.title: What the colour of your clothes says about you
blocks.text:
Some psychologists think that the colour of [1] ______ clothes says a lot about us. They believe that red, purple, or grey clothes give people [2] ______ impressions of what we are like.

Red clothes attract attention and suggest that the wearer is [3] ______. Red is one of the [4] ______ colours to wear when you want to impress or persuade someone to do something for [5] ______. Black and blue are a bit [6] ______ impressive than red, but they also suggest power. Black is more serious than the other two and suggests the wearer is confident and ambitious. If you are going to a job interview, you should probably wear blue, as it shows that you are [7] ______ and can be trusted. People who are optimistic generally wear [8] ______ brighter colours like pink, orange, or yellow. Purple indicates elegance, style, and [9] ______ talent — it’s a colour often worn by artists. Grey is the [10] ______ neutral of all the colours. Grey clothes suggest that a person doesn’t like attracting attention and would rather be on their own.

blocks.title: 4. Read the article. Choose a, b, or c
blocks.instructions: Choose the correct word for each numbered gap.

items.prompt: the colour of ______ clothes
items.explanation: Use our before the noun clothes.

items.prompt: give people ______ impressions
items.explanation: Different is the adjective before impressions.

items.prompt: suggest that the wearer is ______
items.explanation: Red clothes suggest that the wearer is powerful.

items.prompt: one of the ______ colours to wear
items.explanation: Use one of the best + plural noun.

items.prompt: do something for ______
items.explanation: After for, use the object pronoun you.

items.prompt: a bit ______ impressive than red
items.explanation: Use less before an adjective in a comparison.

items.prompt: it shows that you are ______ and can be trusted
items.explanation: Reliable means that you can be trusted.

items.prompt: wear ______ brighter colours
items.explanation: Much can intensify a comparative adjective: much brighter.

items.prompt: elegance, style, and ______ talent
items.explanation: Artists are associated with creative talent.

items.prompt: the ______ neutral of all the colours
items.explanation: Use the most + adjective for a superlative.
